A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FlatQuant and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Their content can be reliably matched across reformatting, renumbering, and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original quantization experiments, including perplexity, question-answering accuracy, MT-Bench evaluations, inference timings, and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds DeepSeek evaluations, additional ablations, mixed-precision results, and memory and latency measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the Kronecker-product parameterization, blockwise MSE objective, scaling and clipping components, SVD/AMP training, and fused kernels. Replacing the terminology 'Kronecker decomposition' with 'Kronecker product' clarifies the existing construction; the added experiments do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: v3 adds C-Eval, MMLU, and AIME2024 evaluations using DeepSeek-V3-Base and DeepSeek-R1 (Table 9), materially broadening task coverage. Existing language-modeling, commonsense QA, MT-Bench, and calibration-source coverage is retained; Qwen evaluations were already present in v2.

E2.justification: FP8 reference baselines newly appear in the DeepSeek comparisons (v3 Table 9). Existing comparator sets remain unchanged, including the weight-only and clipping comparisons. The new AffineQuant discussion in Appendix C.9 does not introduce another evaluated AffineQuant comparison.

E3.justification: New protocols include selective W8A8 layer configurations, single-layer peak-memory measurements, and LLaMA-3-8B latency sweeps over input and KV-cache lengths (Appendices C.5, C.7–C.8). Section 4.4 also revises the stated flatness measure from MSE to Euclidean distance, without establishing recomputation of the retained curves. Existing calibration and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 Table 16 completes the component ablation with scaling-only, clipping-only, and scaling-plus-clipping conditions without learnable transformations. Table 19 tests selective higher precision, while Tables 20–22 examine memory overhead and latency dependence on sequence length. The earlier flatness curves, calibration-source ablation, and clipping analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting procedure is added or removed.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and matched earlier appendix results retain their numerical values. Added results cover DeepSeek, additional component conditions, mixed precision, memory, and latency; for example, v3 reports DeepSeek-R1 AIME2024 scores of 73.3 for FlatQuant versus 79.8 for FP8. Reported transformation storage also changes from 0.11 MB to 3.41 MB in Section 3.1.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix C.1 defines flatness using MSE against an equal-norm flat vector; v3 Section 4.4 and Figure 7 specify Euclidean distance and its sum across tensors. This revises the mathematical definition, although nearby prose still says MSE. The Kronecker identities, SVD reasoning, and resource formulas are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain learnable per-layer affine flattening, less than 1% LLaMA-3-70B accuracy loss under W4A4 quantization, and approximately 2.3x prefill and 1.7x decoding speedups. The additional evaluations support these retained claims without redefining the principal contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds a signal-scale preservation explanation for inverse transformations after clipping and expands the expressivity and layer-coverage comparison with AffineQuant (Appendices C.5 and C.9). It also interprets the new experiments as supporting broader applicability and practical efficiency. Appendix E's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 documents the layer groups assigned W8A8 and the batch sizes, sequence lengths, and single-layer setup used in new profiling experiments. The implementation libraries, optimizer, calibration recipe, SVD/AMP details, kernel procedures, calibration timings, and code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references and context concerning pruning, earlier language-model quantization, and quantized reasoning, including LLM-Pruner, Q-BERT, and Liu et al. (2025). It cites SqueezeLLM in the mixed-precision discussion and expands its positioning against AffineQuant in Appendix C.9, while retaining the existing core positioning.

P1.justification: The exposition is substantially reorganized: flatness analysis moves from Appendix C.1 into Section 4.4, while MT-Bench, weight-only, and transferred-quantization discussions move into Appendix C. Overhead analysis moves into the restructured implementation appendix. Terminology and explanatory prose are also revised, especially the description of the Kronecker construction.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch to a two-column conference layout, with widespread resizing and repositioning of displays. v3 compresses the main ablation table, supplies an expanded appendix version, and adds DeepSeek, mixed-precision, memory, and length-sweep tables. The earlier appendix Figure 8 becomes main-text Figure 7.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens evidence for the affine component through previously missing controls (Table 16) and better documents practical efficiency through memory and sequence-length profiling (Tables 20–22). DeepSeek evaluations broaden empirical support, but their protocol remains sparsely documented, and Section 4.4 retains inconsistent MSE-versus-Euclidean wording. These provide a limited net improvement over v2's already extensive, largely retained evidence.
